name: json-interface
description: An ordinary small job — bump a version constant, then run the suite — driven through each engine's machine-readable interface instead of its human one: `haikode --json` and `opencode run --format json`.
proves: that a script can drive the agent. Every non-blank line of stdout has to parse as a JSON object with a type, the tool calls have to be recoverable from that stream by name, and the final answer has to be readable from it — one line of banner or progress text and `while read line; do … | jq; done` is broken. The filesystem checks are there so this measures a real turn and not an empty well-formed stream.
notes: The runner is driven through its scripted interface for this task regardless of --haikode-mode: the driver's own JSONL would be measuring the harness rather than haikode.
prompt: Bump the version in `app/version.py` from 0.9.0 to 1.0.0, then run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` to prove the suite passes. End your reply with the new version string on a line of its own.

pre_checks.label: the suite really does fail before the run

checks.label: every line of stdout is a JSON object with a type
an edit or write tool call is recoverable from the JSON stream
the test run is recoverable from the JSON stream, with its arguments
the final answer is readable from the JSON stream
nothing outside the project was touched
